blindSummary: This state/province registered a +300 % increase in recorded homo/transphobic cases in 2024 — the sharpest percentage rise of any region in the country, though from an extremely small base: it held only 1.44 % of the national case total. Reporting by the regional daily of two historic gender-identity rectification cases here illustrates how minimal the formal trans presence is: one non-binary adult won the region's first court-ordered birth-certificate correction (before a local civil court), and a teacher was among the first trans residents to complete the legal change (new identity documents from 3 February 2020). The statistical alarm is real — the fastest percentage growth in the country — but the absolute numbers remain marginal, and no region-specific legal finding, institutional incident, or enforcement failure was identified beyond the case-volume trend. A 2026 follow-up in the same paper reports homo/transphobic attacks rising a further 16.6 % here in 2025; the registry declined to release regional figures, stating only country-wide totals.
blindSourceSummaries: Press release of the national LGBTQ+ rights organisation's 23rd annual human-rights report on sexual and gender diversity (18 March 2025): homo/transphobia cases rose 78.7 % to 2,847 in 2024 — 23.5 % of all cases recorded in 23 years — the first regression of LGBTQ+ rights since the return of democracy, with roll-backs in all three branches of state; police-space assaults +200 %, hate speech +116.9 %, hate campaigns +80 %, institutional discrimination +63.9 %, media abuses +50 %, while hate killings fell 33.3 %. Trans people made up 39.73 % of 2024 cases (1,131, up 462.69 % year-on-year). The full report's per-region series places this state/province first nationally on rate of increase (+300 %) from a marginal 1.44 % share of the national total.

The regional daily (published in the provincial capital; 11 July 2026) on 12,669 people having rectified name and legal sex nationally under the eight-year-old gender-identity law (64.6 % trans men, 35.1 % trans women, 42 non-binary/intersex 'X' registrations, per civil-registry data obtained by the national LGBTQ+ rights organisation): the article tells this region's two historic cases — the subject of the region's first court ruling granting a non-binary adult's birth-certificate rectification (before the local civil court), and a teacher among the region's first trans men to complete the legal change (new ID from 3 February 2020), who underwent hormones in the provincial capital and a neighbouring city and waits for surgery. Both recount hostile institutional episodes (a school director's remarks blocking the first person's teaching hire; a secret faculty meeting over the second person's social name at a conservative university); registry officials declined to release regional figures, stating only country-wide totals — underscoring how small the registered trans population is in the region.
blindTangential: This region's case figures come from the combined homo/transphobia series of the national LGBTQ+ rights organisation — the +300 % 2024 surge and the 2025 +16.6 % attack rise include homophobic cases and do not isolate trans-specific events.
blindLocalsOnly: The rectification cases are civil-registry matters for residents (birth-certificate/name-marker change under the national gender-identity law, and the waitlist for public transition healthcare one interviewee describes); they evidence a tiny local trans population rather than visitor-facing services.
